analysis:
This batch is documentation only: the CHANGELOG.md head text (older release history, lines 5948-6754, plus a v0.10.13 candidate header in the patch excerpt) and docs/architecture/inference.md patch hunks. No executable source changed, so no control changed here. Unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:0 is a metadata-only record for inference.md with no text.

Security-relevant behavior described by the docs (not verified against the implementing code, which was not supplied):
1. Cluster-onboarding stop counting (inference.md ~453-473). The leading Mac counts asked stops in its setup record (stopsAsked), and the joining Mac ends onboarding when the count grows. This is a local/cluster control-plane availability and consistency feature. It is a possible TB-012/T-059-style availability surface, because a peer or same-UID process that can request a stop could end onboarding. Authentication of the stop request and of the status reply carrying stopsAsked (ClusterControlReply) is not visible here. Older builds ignore the field, which looks fail-open for the joining Mac. The next pass should check the cluster control channel's authentication in the implementing source.
2. Gemma 4 loop-exit-thinking continuation (inference.md ~3255-3286). The scheduler resubmits a continuation containing the prompt plus the generated thought tokens, with the same cache scope, the same sampling and the same stop strings. It is disabled with logprobs and on a cluster pair. The continuation is an ordinary row, so admission, cache salt scoping, deadlines and billing should apply as usual; the doc states usage is the original prompt plus summed completion tokens. Points for source review: that cacheScope is preserved so cross-tenant prefix-cache reuse (T-041) is not widened; that plaintext is not logged (the log line carries only model, type, period, span, tokens and ends_thought); that the continuation is bound to max_tokens and the deadline; and that the 5 s slot-release wait cannot be abused for resource exhaustion. The doc says LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys passes DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING through to the daemon, which is an operator-controlled env passthrough with no new privilege boundary.

No findings: the documentation introduces no concrete regression. The implementation is outside the supplied evidence, so I have not verified that it matches the docs.
